description: Simulate typed input via MU.testTypeText, proving input rules fire through the real handleTextInput path.

tests.description: Typing '> ' at the start of an empty paragraph wraps it in a blockquote
Typing '## ' at the start of an empty paragraph turns it into an h2 heading
Typing a multi-character string leaves the cursor after the last typed character
Typing at a caret inside existing content inserts at that point, not at the start
Backspace right after a shorthand conversion reverts it via undoInputRule, restoring the literal typed text
Typing with a non-collapsed selection replaces the selected range
testTypeKey throws on an unrecognized modifier segment instead of silently degrading to the unmodified key, including 'Mod-' (unsupported) and this codebase's own 'Ctrl-Mod--' subscript binding
tests.action: expect(() => MU.testTypeKey('Mod-Enter')).toThrow(); expect(() => MU.testTypeKey('Bogus-Enter')).toThrow(); expect(() => MU.testTypeKey('Ctrl-Mod--')).toThrow();

tests.description: testTypeKey splits like prosemirror-keymap does, so a bare '-' or a trailing '--' identify '-' as the literal key instead of throwing on a spurious empty-string modifier (does not assert the boolean return -- false means no handler returned true, not that nothing happened, since some commands here dispatch without returning true; see MarkupEditorApp-4dos)
testTypeText skips \r/\n characters instead of inserting them raw, matching what real typing can produce
